findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
findings.body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array (handleNewBooking can set it to null, and several other callers set it to []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws a TypeError, breaking EventManager.create for events using Google Meet location without a destination calendar. The previous code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration.

findings.title: Unrelated organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: This change flips the slug assignment from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}). Organizations are now given a slug exactly when team billing is enabled and denied one when it is disabled, the opposite of the previous behavior, while requestedSlug in metadata still uses the billing-enabled condition. This unrelated change can break organization creation/routing depending on the billing flag.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback can never find the destination calendar
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, the fallback searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId (the falsy value), so it can never match and returns undefined. updateEvent then calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the booking's destination calendar as before, and deleteEvent has the same dead fallback at line 315. Reschedules/location updates for Google bookings without an externalCalendarId will fail or target the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Lark events for collective hosts always use the first host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent ignores the credential being processed and always uses destinationCalendar[0]. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents loops over every collective host's destination calendar and calls createEvent once per credential, so for the second and later hosts Lark will try to create the event on the organizer's calendar ID using another host's credentials, which will fail or write to the wrong calendar. Google was changed to select the destination matching credentialId, but Lark (and similarly Office365 at CalendarService.ts:73 and CalDAV at packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) was only converted to read the first array element.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to result.credentialId only for calendar results and undefined for everything else. Previously video results kept result.credentialId. Dedicated video meetings (e.g. Zoom/Meet alternatives stored as *_video references) will now be persisted with credentialId undefined, so cancellation/update flows that look up the specific video credential by reference.credentialId cannot find it and may not delete/update the video meeting.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: When newBookingId is provided, the cleanup uses booking.references.find(...) to locate a single old calendar reference and deletes only that one event. Collective bookings now have multiple calendar references (one per host), so the old events on the other hosts' calendars are never deleted on reschedule, leaving orphaned duplicate events. It should iterate all old *_calendar references, as updateAllCalendarEvents now does for updates.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective handling then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). In that case the optional chain silently skips the push, so team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are lost and those hosts receive no calendar event. It should initialize an array (or assign teamDestinationCalendars) instead of relying on push.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only first reference per booking, repeatedly
findings.body: Inside the new loop over every calendar reference, the recurring branch maps over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and for each updated booking picks updBooking.references.find(...) - only the first calendar reference. With multiple collective hosts/references this both repeats the same deletion pass once per outer reference (duplicate delete calls pushed into apiDeletes) and still misses the non-first calendar events of each recurring booking, leaving them on other hosts' calendars after cancellation.
